title: Hutchinson was Milan's hero, not me – Amorim
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutHutchinson was Milan's hero, not me – AmorimShareAC Milan overturned a two-goal deficit to beat Olympiacos in the Europa League on Thursday, but Ruben Amorim refused to take any credit.Ruben Amorim said Omari Hutchinson deserved more credit for turning the game in AC Milan's favour than he did, after the Rossoneri recovered from two goals down to beat Olympiacos.
Milan were staring at what would have been a fourth defeat in five Europa League matches this season, with a Mike Maignan own goal and Jota Silva's strike putting the Greek side on top.
However, Hutchinson scored and provided assists for Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic, before Diego Moreira made the result certain in second-half stoppage time.

It is the first time in the Rossoneri's illustrious history that they have conceded multiple goals in three straight matches in major European competitions, yet Hutchinson's heroics – which also included creating a team-high three chances – helped them to a crucial victory.
And afterwards, Amorim played down the idea that his substitutions, which included the half-time withdrawal of Goncalo Ramos, had been the catalyst for Milan's fightback.
"I always expected this from him. He has the potential to do much more. He has talent, like other players in the squad, but it's the head that counts," Amorim said of Hutchinson.
"I didn't change the game. Ramos came off because he was in pain, so it was a normal substitution.
"Hutchinson changed the game more than I did. What changed it was the first goal."

Milan now sit 20th in the league-phase standings. They are only inside the play-off qualification places on goal difference, and with three games to play, four points separate them from the top eight.
And Amorim admitted taking all three points was always going to be important if Milan were to harbour any realistic hopes of qualifying automatically for the round of 16.
"It definitely changes our future. We did well in the second half, but we made a lot of mistakes again, and we still have to improve," Amorim said.
"We have a lot to do to become a very strong team, but the spirit is there. This is the start of something."
Milan can now turn their focus back to Serie A ahead of Monday's trip to Cagliari, with the Rossoneri only losing one of their opening 12 games to sit fourth in the table.
